cohort: Six supplement products selected incrementally from user-supplied current-use names and package panels

method.observation: Manual read-only inspection of public manufacturer and retailer pages in Safari
method.privacy: The screenshot was used only to select product cases and serving forms. It is not committed, and no intake frequency, schedule or health purpose is retained.
method.mutations: None; no basket, order, review, subscription or account action
method.promotion_rule: Public values are resolution candidates, not measured values. Exact current physical-package evidence is required before promotion to measured.

interpretation: The cohort validates supplement-specific identity, compound, dose-form and serving-basis requirements but does not create intake events or a supplement catalogue. No observed page supplies an immutable release or formulation-effective date. The five user-supplied labels (a multivitamin tablet, a fish-oil softgel, a zinc capsule, a vitamin drop product and a psyllium powder) are evidence-scoped package authority: the multivitamin directly measures 24 canonical micronutrients per tablet, the fish oil measures fish-oil concentrate, EPA and DHA per two softgels and supports an exact one-softgel projection, the zinc product measures 15 mg elemental zinc per capsule while retaining its compound provenance, the drop product measures its printed six-drop values and supports an exact one-drop projection, and the psyllium powder separates component mass from supplied fibre at a direct 3.16 g basis. Their raw images remain local-only. Public pages may corroborate candidates, but malformed retailer rows, source-specific RI/Daily Value percentages, a 1.7-versus-1.65 mg thiamin difference, image-only labels, removed pages and a public psyllium mass-versus-fibre conflict demonstrate why current package evidence remains authoritative.
